podcast-dannyjones-xQOWXfDIUzM:
Journalist David Holthouse tells Danny Jones about a cartel-linked triple murder known as the Sasquatch case. Holthouse is a true-crime writer known for going deep into dark scenes and coming back with strange stories. He says he was close to the events he describes here.

Holthouse walks through the killings and the odd Sasquatch lore wrapped around them. He explains how cartel money, remote land, and local myth mixed into one grim tale. Jones pushes for what Holthouse saw himself and what he only heard. Brave listeners get a true-crime story stranger than most fiction.
podcast-joerogan-6si_KIa9yZM:
Researcher Julia Mossbridge brings the science of precognition to episode 2496 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Mossbridge studies whether people can sense future events before they happen. Her lab work reports small but stubborn effects that standard science struggles to explain.

Mossbridge explains her experiments on intuition and the body's early responses to coming events. She is careful about what the data does and does not prove. Rogan asks about time itself and whether the future can leak into the present. Open-minded listeners get a serious scientist making a strange claim with data in hand.
podcast-joerogan-Cz6AO391KZM:
The COVID relief bill and the origins of the coronavirus share a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience from the pandemic's height. Rogan works through the news of that week: a giant spending bill moving through Congress, and a virus whose source was still hotly argued.

He questions what the bill held besides relief, and why so much was packed into one vote. On the virus, he weighs the market story against the lab story as the evidence then stood. The segment is a time-stamped record of how the pandemic's politics sounded while events were still unfolding.
podcast-joerogan-q1Eso459GZM:
Comic Sam Tripoli brings his conspiracy-loving act to episode 2218 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Tripoli hosts the Tin Foil Hat podcast, where no official story goes unchallenged. With Rogan, a fellow skeptic of tidy answers, the talk runs wild by design.

Tripoli riffs through secret societies, hidden history, and the wildest claims he covers on his own show. Rogan laughs, pushes back, and adds his own favorite mysteries. The tone stays comic even when the topics turn dark. Listeners get a tour of modern conspiracy culture from one of its most cheerful tour guides.
